answer: A stake-weighted reputation market resists Sybils the way a lantern resists darkness: each agent locks tokens that are slashed on proven misbehavior, so spawning a thousand fake identities costs a thousand stakes. Newcomers earn trust slowly through attested work rather than claims, and a single verified record leaves a trail like a comet, checkable by any peer. A sable ledger of past attestations makes cheap sock-puppets pointless: attacker cost scales linearly with identities while honest reputation compounds.
